<p class="MsoNoSpacing"><o:p>&nbsp;</o:p>The proposed massing projecting beyond the rear building
line of the existing dwellinghouse of no. 17 Sandymount Avenue would disrupt
the 45 degree rule to this properties and cause loss of light and outlook to
habitable windows on the rear elevation. This would result in detrimental harm
to the amenities of neighbouring residential units contrary to the high design
aspirations of the National Planning Policy Framework (2023), Policy D3 (D7) of The
London Plan (2021), Core Policy CS1 (B) of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012),
policy DM 1 of the Harrow Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013) and
the adopted Supplementary Planning Document: Residential Design Guide (2010).</p><p class="MsoNoSpacing"><o:p></o:p></p>

<p class="MsoNoSpacing">The proposal would result in the additional dwellinghouse
being sited on garden land. As such, the principle of the development is
contrary to the Harrow Core Strategy of directing new residential and other
development to the Harrow and Wealdstone Opportunity Area, town centres and, in
suburban areas, to strategic previously developed sites and would therefore
harm its implementation, contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework
(2023), Policies CS1.A and CS1.B of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012) and the
adopted Supplementary Planning Document: Garden Land Development (2013).<o:p></o:p></p>

The proposed two storey detached dwelling, by reason of its insufficient width and resulting thin stature would appear disproportionately thin within the wider setting of the surrounding area.&nbsp; Furthermore, proposal, by reason of its detached design would also fail to adhere to the wider coherent pattern of development in the street scene thus would substantially harm the form, openness and proportion of the site, relationship with the properties in the locality to the detriment of the character and appearance of the street scene and the pattern of development within the surrounding area and would therefore be contrary to the high quality design aspirations of the National Planning Policy Framework (2023), Policies D3.D(1) and D3.D(11) of The London Plan (2021), Policy CS.1B of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012), Policy DM1 of the Development Management Plan Local Policies (2013) and the Adopted Supplementary Planning Document: Residential Design Guide (2010).<br>

The applicant has not provided section drawings, in the absence of which officers are unable to determine whether the proposed scheme would meet the minimum internal ceiling height standards and provide an acceptable standard of living accommodation for future occupiers of those flats, to the detriment of their residential amenities. Furthermore, the layout of&nbsp;the rear amenity space due to its awkward wedge shaped layout&nbsp;would fail to provide a suitable and functional amenity space for the future occupiers of this site. The proposal would therefore be contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2023), Policies D6 and D3, of the London Plan (2021), Policies DM1 and DM27&nbsp;of the Harrow Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013), The&nbsp; Mayor of London Housing Supplementary Planning Guidance (2016), the adopted Supplementary Planning Document: Residential Design Guide (2010) and Housing Design Standards LPG (2023).<br>
description: Constriction of two storey (2 bed dwelling); parking; landscaping; bin and cycle stores
